newsitem.title: USA: Stock market lower ahead of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stock market lower ahead of Fed meeting.

text.p: Stock prices moved lower Monday as technology shares suffered another pounding, while the blue-chip market was cautious ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate setting group.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 4.15 points at 6,800.64, and the Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, tumbled 15.46 points to 1,238.61.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances by a 13-8 margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 243 million shares.
The overall market appeared to have already discounted a quarter-point increase in short-term interest rates from the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee.
The Fed policy-makers meet at 9 a.m. Eastern time (1400 GMT) Tuesday and following recent practice, the result of the meeting should be known around 2:15 p.m. (1915 GMT).
In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond rose more than a quarter point, and its yield fell to 6.94 percent from Friday's close of 6.97 percent.
Analysts said a correction in high technology stocks has extended to such superstars as Microsoft Corp. and Intel Corp., which means that it may be drawing to an end.
"The techs were overowned and overbought and headed for a shakeout," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Microsoft, the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, tumbled 4-1/2 to 89-1/2, Intel was down 2-1/4 at 128-1/4, Hewlett-Packard fell 1-1/2 to 55-1/8, but International Business Machines Corp. was up 7/8 at 133-1/4.
"The correction in techs is following a natural course," said Tony O'Bryan, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
"The correction started in stocks which were fundamentally defective or deficient and then moved onto small-caps and mid-caps," he said. "Now you are correcting the big boys like Intel and Microsoft.

"While it looks nasty, it is showing me that we are in a mature phase of the correction in techs because it has run the gamut," O'Bryan said. "The good news is that once the leaders stop correcting, the correction will be over. We will have a good trading rally. But this correction may last several hours or days."
He said investors were cautious ahead of the Fed meeting.
"Part of the corrective phase has to do with the possible rate hike," O'Bryan said. "Once it is out of the way, i think the market will start acting much better.
"The positive side is that Greenspan will have taken pre-emptive action and that should help the long end of the bond market, which, in turn, will help stocks," he said.
Among special situations, Medic Computer System Inc. lost 13-7/8 to 14-1/8 after the company said first quarter results would be below Wall Street expectations.
IDEXX Laboratories Inc. plunged 20-1/8 to 11-7/8 after it also said its quarterly earnings would fall significantly below Wall analysts's estimates.
MDL Information Systems Inc. rallied 13-7/8 to 31-1/8 after Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said it had agreed to buy MDL for $320 million.
